content.comment_body: Hello everyone, here is my situation: I have three analog threshold switches monitoring the same analog input (temperature). Each switch controls a separate heating system, but they must follow a specific activation order determined by the first heating's settings. - The first switch should power on below temperature (x) and turn off above temperature (y). - The second should power on below (z = x+5) and turn off above (k = y-5). - The third should power on below (z+2) and turn off above (k-2). I've noticed that direct formula use in the threshold switch isn't possible. I did find the 'mathematical operation' function, but it doesn't allow using the ON value as a reference since only the Ax value is accepted. Any suggestions for linking the ON/OFF values?
I'm familiar with connecting the switches, but I can't reference the ON values in a formula as I'd like.
You can resolve this using VM mapping.
Alternatively, you could try this approach.
Thanks, using an approach similar to the second suggestion solved my issue.

In [product_name] software, just below a block, there is a small gray square with a '+' symbol. Clicking it brings up a 'Reference' block. You can connect references similarly to standard connections. Some reference blocks feature a '+' to the right of the reference value, allowing you to change the time base (seconds, minutes, hours).

analysis.insight_summary: Users face limitations when configuring analog threshold switches, as ON/OFF thresholds cannot be directly referenced or calculated using formulas. Although workarounds like VM mapping and reference blocks exist, they are not straightforward and demand manual setup. This absence of dynamic formula referencing creates inefficiencies and increases the risk of setup mistakes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users would like to dynamically assign ON/OFF threshold values, referencing other variables or using formulas within the configuration interface, to improve setup automation and efficiency.
